findings.title: Replay ZIP fails its recorded integrity hash

evidence.detail: Manifest claims f35fa6e7… for replay.zip; actual archive SHA256 is 7d6514db…. All six ZIP member CRCs pass and each member matches the site counterpart, including artifact-manifest.json itself.

findings.impact: A consumer validating the published bundle against its manifest must reject the archive. Including the manifest inside the archive while the manifest also hashes that archive creates a circular packaging dependency, or preserves a stale prior archive hash. This is a packaging defect, not a numerical-result mismatch.
findings.recommendation: Keep the inner content manifest limited to payload files; build the ZIP afterward; record the archive hash in a separate outer checksum record that is not included inside that ZIP. Rebuild from recorded evidence without rerunning decisions.

findings.title: The checked-in renderer cannot reproduce the new Jev site

evidence.detail: Unchanged local renderer enumerates exact/Qwen/Qwen+Qwen/Qwen+Laya, fixes the illustrative pair and plots to exact, and copies the older visualization/index.html.
New site contains pilot-03, five arms including Jev, defaultArm=jev and pre-exchange event snapshots.
Manifest still labels mapping H1-retrospective-recorded, whereas the frozen pilot-03 plan specifies H2.

findings.impact: Running the available local renderer on the now-complete pilot-03 export would omit Jev from effects and overwrite the new Jev UI/plots with the older exact-control presentation. The record is externally recoverable via pinned source, but the workspace build is not reproducible.
findings.recommendation: Import the exact matching renderer/template from the recorded source revision or make the renderer data-driven over manifest arms and the predeclared illustrative-pair rule. Record the renderer/template hash and H2 mapping. Verify the rebuilt site against the unchanged 180-world dataset.

findings.title: Recovery zero now hides a real damage-and-exchange interval

evidence.detail: All three erasure-only sharing trajectories report recovery_rounds=0. New snapshots show 40 empty memories, pre-exchange atlas accuracy85%/coverage84%; the first exchange raises atlas accuracy to95% and coverage93–94%.

findings.impact: The established metric defines zero as first qualifying post-exchange frame at round10, not zero exchanges or no damage. The new telemetry makes that distinction observable. Without a phase label, the recovery number can be mistaken for instantaneous/no-loss recovery. The remaining task perturbation is small: only0.357 percentage points additional integrated atlas error relative to no event.
findings.recommendation: Preserve the historical metric, label it first qualifying recorded round offset, and additionally report event-phase loss plus recovery_exchanges (first exchange=1). Include pre-exchange and post-exchange phase names wherever the recovery result is displayed.

findings.title: Pilot03 qualification prose miscounts distinct method names

evidence.detail: Plan describes four new method names; source new_qualification uses i=0..19 and names system K401 through K420, with five phrasings/class repeated across20 names.

findings.impact: Small reproducibility/writing error; the actual60 balanced cases and15 semantic templates are intact. Renamed entities do not create60 independent semantic templates.
findings.recommendation: Correct in an explicitly dated erratum:20 method names, five phrasings/class,60 items. Keep the frozen preregistration unchanged and linked.

updated_conclusions: Pilot03 is a valid narrow model-extraction reference experiment, with36 exact worlds and36 Jev worlds complete and108 Qwen-derived worlds explicitly not run. It is not a successful Qwen swarm or heterogeneous-head study.

Jev fresh qualification is60/60;600 pilot extraction labels match the exact tape across all three corpora. Therefore the downstream equality between Jev and exact is expected. It validates this narrow semantic interface, not general fact verification or independent replication across600 semantic tasks.

Forwarding withdrawal notices reduced mean integrated combined-scenario atlas error by28.095 percentage points versus local notices (three paired seeds:28.929,30.357,25.000 points). Withdrawal-only has the same effect. Final propagated-notice atlas accuracy is100% with zero stale citations in these worlds.

All660 attempts returned on typesafe/jev-1.13-20260917 through TypeSafe, with283,626 recorded input tokens and USD0.011912292 model usage for this attempt. Every started call has one terminal; zero provider failures.

All72 recorded trajectories, final memory states and pre-exchange snapshots replay byte-for-structure from frozen corpora/tapes using matching pinned simulation source. All1,728 retained frames and24 paired-effect records reconcile, and all180 embedded site worlds match raw outcomes.

The new site and representative PNGs clearly identify Jev reference, programmed propagation, missing Qwen-derived conditions and evaluator-only coloring. The always-uncertain comparator is appropriately labeled a post-hoc sanity check. No image evidence suggests fabricated transitions.
